per_token_ms.note: wall was ~768 ms/token in this window (profile eventSync + fprintf overhead inflate it; serving wall is ~714)

derived.hit_copy_diagnosis: 474 slabs x 3 cudaMemcpy = 1422 calls at ~62-65us/call -> call-overhead dominated, not bandwidth (4.4 GB at only 47 GB/s)
derived.fetch_diagnosis: 1.54 GB/token at ~7.2 GB/s aggregate; per-layer lines show ~1.05 ms per single miss (3x 3.1MB reads) — near the drive's random ceiling for 3.1MB granularity; 9.3MB contiguous slab reads would reach ~12.5 GB/s (QD sweep)
derived.kernel_diagnosis: gateup+down read 5.86 GB/token of expert weights at ~55 GB/s effective — this 107 ms is the floor that remains even at 100% hit rate with zero copies
derived.decode_ceiling_faithful: ~6-8 t/s with every loader cost removed (kernels + attention/dense remain); consistent with research doc's 5.5-9. Only levers past it: fewer bytes/token (MTP drafting multiplier) or faster kernel read path

ranked_next_levers_by_measured_value: 1. async/batched hit copies + fills (92.5+34.5 -> ~20 ms; ~30 lines, no kernel changes) then re-measure before deciding on full zero-copy pointer-indirection

3. GGUF slab repack (gate|up|down contiguous per expert): fetch granularity 3.1 -> 9.3 MB, ~7.2 -> ~11-12.5 GB/s
4. GLM MTP block / drafting: multiplies effective t/s by accept length across the ENTIRE per-token cost — the only lever that beats the byte-arithmetic ceiling
5. kernel read-path bandwidth (55 GB/s effective vs ~200 attainable) — investigate before writing new kernels
